newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal CEO sees 97 net up 15-17 pct.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal CEO sees 97 net up 15-17 pct.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc now expects earnings to show a 15 to 17 percent increase in 1997, Chief Executive Officer Lawrence Bossidy told Reuters Wednesday.

Earlier, the company reported second quarter earnings to $305 million, or $1.08 a share, saying this was up 16 percent over comparable 1996 net income and pointing out it was the company's 22nd consecutive quarter of earnings growth of 14 percent or more.
First half earnings were also up 16 percent, to $564 million, or $1.99 per share, AlliedSignal said.
The First Call consensus for the latest quarter was $1.08.
These analysts are now projecting a 20 percent rise in annual earnings per share to $4.20.

The company said sales in the second quarter were $3.6 billion, an increase of 7 percent over the second quarter of 1996. Although foreign exchange and labor strikes at two major customers reduced second-quarter sales by a total of 2 percent, sales increased 10 percent in Aerospace, 7 percent in Engineered Materials and 2 percent in Automotive, where safety restraint system sales were hurt by strikes at General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp.

"We are very happy with our second quarter," Bossidy said in a telephone interview, pointing out it came on balanced growth, noting operating margin in the second quarter expanded to a record 12.0 percent from 11.4 percent in the year-earlier quarter.

"Outstanding internal sales growth in Aerospace, Engineered Materials, Turbocharging Systems and Truck Brake Systems was augmented by rapid progress in our accelerated productivity initiatives, including our maturing Six Sigma efforts," said Bossidy.
"Many of our businesses are growing at multiples of the economic growth rates in our global markets," he said.

"In addition, our continued ability to reduce costs and expand factory throughput while increasing sales gives us a high degree of confidence that we'll achieve our goal of 15-to-17 percent earnings growth for 1997 despite the second-quarter moderation of U.S. GDP growth."
Globally, he added, "we don't see much in the way of inflation," explaining there have been no price pressures from suppliers.
He also noted the French and German economies "are slowly getting better."
Asked about the $1.5 billion in cash and short-term investments AlliedSignal had at June 30, he noted the company agreed to three acquisitions in the second quarter and closed two of them.
"We have more acquisitions in the pipeline," he added.
